newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products-mogas, HS fuel steady, others weak.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products-mogas, HS fuel steady, others weak.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were either steady or weaker on Monday.

Naphtha took a breather after falling $14 to six-month lows on Friday. However, despite the lull in trade today sentiment remained bearish with crude staying volatile to the downside and end-user buying for Naphtha relaxed.
Traders said closed arbitrage options out of the region were also weighing on prices. Cargoes were valued around $190 cif Med but buyers and sellers were around $3 apart.
Gasoline held steady with tight supplies supporting cargoes prices around $216-$217 a tonne cif Lavera.
Traders said recent good buying interest for West Africa had drawn heavily on supplies but this was balanced by slack local demand.

Gas oil had a slow day amid prices up to $3 a tonne weaker. Russian material was still tight for this week, but nearly all interest was for fob material rather than cif. On a cif basis traders heard talk around cif high quotes +50-75 cents.
The majority of players, however, were preferring non Russian 0.2 percent heating oil and prepared to pay up to fob high quotes +$3.50, a touch off the "optimistic" +$4 talked on Friday.
High sulphur fuel oil was stable. A refiner bought 45,000 tonnes of bunker material, loading in mid-March, from a trader. The deal was concluded half at $90 cif Med and half on a floating basis.
Low sulphur cracked fuel oil was weaker, under pressure from avails across the Atlantic.
Russian material remains scarce although dealers said they saw some avails of high and low sulphur material out of Novorossiisk.
